motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the Consent Agenda, moving item 12.B. to the scheduled items for further discussion, and amending the effective date for item 13.B. to the date of closing. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Approve the routine consent items in one vote
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulling one item out for separate discussion and changing another item's effective date to the date of closing.
motions.impact: Routine housekeeping — this is the batch of items council members agreed needed no debate. Nothing here changes for residents.

motions.item_title: Table the Eagle Square Commercial Preliminary Plat
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to table the Eagle Square Commercial Preliminary Plat. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Delay the Eagle Square commercial plans
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on the preliminary plat — the proposed lot layout — for the Eagle Square commercial development.
motions.impact: Nothing is approved or blocked yet; the project returns on a later agenda. No change for residents in the meantime.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the First Amendment to the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Annual Budget
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the First Amendment to the Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Annual Budget. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Amend this year's city budget
motions.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the city's 2024-2025 annual budget; the motion itself names no dollar figures.
motions.impact: This is a routine mid-year adjustment. The motion does not say what money moved or how much, and nothing changes for residents day to day.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 17.25 Residential Zones, 17.35 Commercial Zones, and 17.37 Business Park Zones with the following change: 1. The amendment in 17.25.050(G), 17.35.050(G), and 17.37.050(G) be amended to read, “No permanent structures near natural washes shall be built in the watercourse plus 75 feet from the center of the flowline, or a 50-foot buffer on either side, as measured out from the top of the wash, whichever is greater, to be determined by the City Engineer or designee. Additionally, no earthwork, excavation, or earth removal shall occur within the watercourse plus 75 feet from the center of the flowline, or a 50-foot buffer on either side of the top-of-bank as determined by determined by the City Engineer or designee.” Councilmember Clark seconded the motion
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 17.25 Residential Zones, 17.35 Commercial Zones, and 17.37 Business Park Zones with the following change: 1. The amendment in 17.25.050(G), 17.35.050(G), and 17.37.050(G) be amended to read, “No permanent structures near natural washes shall be built in the watercourse plus 75 feet from the center of the flowline, or a 50-foot buffer on either side, as measured out from the top of the wash, whichever is greater, to be determined by the City Engineer or designee. Additionally, no earthwork, excavation, or earth removal shall occur within the watercourse plus 75 feet from the center of the flowline, or a 50-foot buffer on either side of the top-of-bank as determined by determined by the City Engineer or designee.” Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Keep buildings and digging back from natural washes
motions.summary: The council took up a rule keeping buildings and earthwork back from natural washes: 75 feet from the flow line's center or 50 feet from the bank, whichever is greater.
motions.impact: If you own or build on a lot beside a natural wash, this would shrink the area you can build or excavate on, with the city engineer setting the exact line.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as the Enyo Battery Property from the Airpark Zone to the Agriculture Zone
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as the Enyo Battery Property from the Airpark Zone to the Agriculture Zone. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rezone the Enyo battery site to agriculture
motions.summary: The council rezoned the land known as the Enyo Battery property out of the airpark zone and into the agriculture zone.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents today. It resets what can be built on that one property going forward.

Equestrian Center be changed from Permitted to Special; b. The Windmills line be amended to include language stating “Windmills, if exclusively secondary/accessory to an AG use”; c. Utility, Public or Private be changed from Permitted to blank; 2. 17.37.020 Land Use Table Utility, Public or Private be changed from Permitted to blank; and 3. 17.38.060(E) retain the maximum of six allowed number of moving vehicles, and include “(e.g., vans, box trucks, trailers, etc.)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code, Repealing and Replacing Chapter 17.40 Industrial Zone, and Amending Chapters 17.20 Agriculture Zone and 17.38 Commercial Storage Zone with the following changes: 1. 17.20.020 Land Use Table: a. Equestrian Center be changed from Permitted to Special; b. The Windmills line be amended to include language stating “Windmills, if exclusively secondary/accessory to an AG use”; c. Utility, Public or Private be changed from Permitted to blank; 2. 17.37.020 Land Use Table Utility, Public or Private be changed from Permitted to blank; and 3. 17.38.060(E) retain the maximum of six allowed number of moving vehicles, and include “(e.g., vans, box trucks, trailers, etc.). Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rewrite industrial zoning; limit windmills and storage
motions.summary: The council replaced the industrial zoning chapter and tightened farm-zone rules: equestrian centers now need special approval, windmills only as farm accessories, storage yards capped at six moving vehicles.
motions.impact: This affects landowners and businesses, not households. An equestrian center on agricultural land now needs special approval, and a commercial storage yard may keep at most six moving vehicles such as vans, box trucks, or trailers.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code to Enact Section 17.60.155 Lot Size Mixture (R Lots)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code to Enact Section 17.60.155 Lot Size Mixture (R Lots). Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Delay new rules on mixing lot sizes
motions.summary: The council put off a decision on a proposed rule requiring a mixture of lot sizes in residential development.
motions.impact: No change for now. If the rule comes back and passes, it would mainly shape how builders lay out lots in new neighborhoods.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.10 Definitions, and Sections 16.35.090 Privacy Fencing, 17.60.120 General Fencing Provisions, and 17.60.130 Chain Link Fencing
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.10 Definitions, and Sections 16.35.090 Privacy Fencing, 17.60.120 General Fencing Provisions, and 17.60.130 Chain Link Fencing. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rewrite the rules on fences, including chain link
motions.summary: The council considered rewriting the city's fence rules, covering privacy fences, general fencing standards, chain link fencing, and the definitions behind them.
motions.impact: If you plan to put up a fence, these rules decide what you can build. The motion does not spell out what changed, so check the current code with the city before you buy materials.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as the Berry Property
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as the Berry Property. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Update the land use map for the Berry Property
motions.summary: The council took up a change to the city's long-range land use map for the Berry Property; the record does not show how the vote ended.
motions.impact: This is the map-keeping half of the Berry Property rezoning — paperwork that keeps the city's long-range plan lined up with its zoning. Nothing changes day to day.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as the Berry Property from Agriculture to Foothill Residential
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as the Berry Property from Agriculture to Foothill Residential. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rezone the Berry Property for foothill homes
motions.summary: The council rezoned the Berry Property from agriculture to foothill residential, opening land previously set aside for farming to housing.
motions.impact: If you live near this land, expect homes rather than farmland here in time. The vote does not approve any specific project, builder, or number of houses.
